meta.role_gating_note: V4-P4: per-stage `intro` became a per-role record (was a single flat string) so the roadmap speaks to what the selected track's day-to-day actually looks like, not generic phrasing. `certPaths` is new — a static, ordered 'typical certification path' per role, reusing the certification-progression research already done for V3-P0's corpus weighting (data/corpus.json's role_weighting_note and AGENT_STATE.md's V3-P0 research notes): CompTIA's Security+ -> CySA+ progression for SOC, Network+ -> CCNA for Network Security Engineer, eJPT as the truer entry VAPT cert with OSCP flagged as a later/aspirational step (not required), and ISC2 CC as the least track-differentiated true-beginner cert for Generalist. Shown as static reference context alongside the gap-driven stages, not as a gap-driven action itself — someone can be fully caught up on every stage and still want to know 'what's the standard cert path for my track.'

vapt: OSCP (later, once you have hands-on experience)

intro.soc_analyst: Start here — SIEM-driven log analysis and networking reasoning are the daily bread of a SOC analyst, so get these solid before anything else.
intro.vapt: Start here — networking fundamentals and core security concepts underpin every finding you'll later need to explain in a pentest report.
intro.network_security_engineer: Start here — TCP/IP, routing, and core security concepts are the foundation everything else on this roadmap builds on.
intro.generalist: Start here — core concepts, log analysis, and networking reasoning underpin everything else on this roadmap.

stages.title: Get hands-on with tools and real scenarios

intro.soc_analyst: Next, turn concepts into muscle memory — SIEM tool practice plus the incident-response and OWASP-awareness reasoning you'll use on every shift.
intro.vapt: Next, turn concepts into muscle memory — hands-on tool practice (scanning, exploitation, reporting) plus vulnerability and OWASP reasoning.
intro.network_security_engineer: Next, turn concepts into muscle memory — firewall and router configuration practice plus the vulnerability and incident awareness that comes with defending a network.
intro.generalist: Next, turn concepts into muscle memory — hands-on tool practice plus vulnerability, OWASP, and incident-response reasoning.

intro.soc_analyst: With the fundamentals in place, a certification is the fastest way to signal SOC-analyst readiness to recruiters and ATS filters.
intro.vapt: With the fundamentals in place, a certification is the fastest way to signal pentesting readiness to recruiters and ATS filters.
intro.network_security_engineer: With the fundamentals in place, a certification is the fastest way to signal network-security readiness to recruiters and ATS filters.
intro.generalist: With the fundamentals in place, a certification is the fastest way to make your skills legible to recruiters and ATS filters.

intro.soc_analyst: Basic scripting (PowerShell especially) lets you automate log triage and stands out even at fresher level.
intro.vapt: Basic scripting (Python especially) lets you automate repetitive testing steps and stands out even at fresher level.
intro.network_security_engineer: Basic scripting lets you automate config checks and repetitive network tasks — a real differentiator at fresher level.
intro.generalist: Basic scripting lets you automate the repetitive parts of the job and stands out even at fresher level.

intro.soc_analyst: Finally, make sure your CV actually shows the shift-based, detail-oriented soft skills SOC hiring managers screen for.
intro.vapt: Finally, make sure your CV actually shows the reporting and communication skills that separate a good pentester from a good hacker.
intro.network_security_engineer: Finally, make sure your CV actually shows the reliability and documentation habits network teams screen for.
intro.generalist: Finally, make sure your CV actually shows the soft skills hiring managers screen for, not just technical ones.
